pattern.title: One Word Substitution
pattern.description: A single word for a phrase.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A person who scientifically studies the stars, planets and other celestial bodies"
questions.explanation: The word is "astronomer": one who scientifically studies stars, planets and other celestial bodies. The other options mean: astrologer: one who predicts human fortunes and events from the positions of stars; geologist: a scientist who studies the earth's rocks and structure; meteorologist: a scientist who studies weather and the atmosphere.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A person who hates women"
questions.explanation: The word is "misogynist": a person who hates women. The other options mean: misanthrope: a person who hates or distrusts mankind; philanderer: a man who has casual love affairs with many women; bigot: a person who is intolerantly attached to his own opinions.

questions.questionText: Which one word stands for "A person who hates or distrusts mankind"?
questions.explanation: The word is "misanthrope": a person who hates or distrusts mankind. The other options mean: misogynist: a person who hates women; philanthropist: a person who loves mankind and helps it through charity; pessimist: a person who expects the worst.

questions.questionText: What is the one-word substitute for: "A person who loves mankind and works for its welfare through charity"?
questions.explanation: The word is "philanthropist": a person who loves mankind and helps it through charity. The other options mean: misanthrope: a person who hates or distrusts mankind; cynic: a person who distrusts the motives of others; hermit: a person who lives alone, away from society.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A lover and collector of books"
questions.explanation: The word is "bibliophile": a lover and collector of books. The other options mean: philatelist: a collector and student of postage stamps; numismatist: a collector or student of coins and medals; lexicographer: one who compiles dictionaries.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A person who collects postage stamps as a hobby"
questions.explanation: The word is "philatelist": a collector and student of postage stamps. The other options mean: numismatist: a collector or student of coins and medals; bibliophile: a lover and collector of books; antiquarian: a collector or student of antiques and ancient objects.
questions.shortcut: Phil- = love; ateleia = freedom from tax (postage stamp).

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A person who writes in shorthand"
questions.explanation: The word is "stenographer": one who writes in shorthand. The other options mean: calligrapher: an expert in beautiful handwriting; cryptographer: one who writes or designs secret codes; typographer: one who designs or arranges printed type.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A doctor who specialises in diseases of the eye"
questions.explanation: The word is "ophthalmologist": a doctor who specialises in diseases of the eye. The other options mean: cardiologist: a doctor who specialises in diseases of the heart; neurologist: a doctor who specialises in diseases of the nerves and brain; dermatologist: a doctor who specialises in diseases of the skin.

questions.questionText: Which one word stands for "A doctor who specialises in diseases of the heart"?
questions.explanation: The word is "cardiologist": a doctor who specialises in diseases of the heart. The other options mean: pulmonologist: a doctor who specialises in diseases of the lungs; neurologist: a doctor who specialises in diseases of the nerves and brain; dermatologist: a doctor who specialises in diseases of the skin.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A doctor who treats the diseases of children"
questions.explanation: The word is "paediatrician": a doctor who treats children's diseases. The other options mean: geriatrician: a doctor who treats the diseases of old people; gynaecologist: a doctor who treats women's reproductive health; dermatologist: a doctor who specialises in diseases of the skin.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A scientist who studies birds"
questions.explanation: The word is "ornithologist": a scientist who studies birds. The other options mean: entomologist: a scientist who studies insects; herpetologist: a scientist who studies reptiles and amphibians; ichthyologist: a scientist who studies fish.

questions.questionText: What is the one-word substitute for: "A person who travels on foot"?
questions.explanation: The word is "pedestrian": a person who travels on foot. The other options mean: pilgrim: a person who journeys to a sacred place; passenger: a person who travels in a vehicle without driving it; nomad: a member of a tribe that moves from place to place in search of pasture.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A person who always looks on the bright side and expects the best"
questions.explanation: The word is "optimist": a person who always expects the best and looks on the bright side. The other options mean: pessimist: a person who expects the worst; cynic: a person who distrusts the motives of others; sceptic: a person who doubts accepted opinions.

questions.questionText: Which one word stands for "A person who collects or studies coins and medals"?
questions.explanation: The word is "numismatist": a collector or student of coins and medals. The other options mean: philatelist: a collector and student of postage stamps; cartographer: one who draws or makes maps; lexicographer: one who compiles dictionaries.

questions.questionText: What is the one-word substitute for: "A person who draws or makes maps"?
questions.explanation: The word is "cartographer": one who draws or makes maps. The other options mean: lexicographer: one who compiles dictionaries; stenographer: one who writes in shorthand; biographer: one who writes the life story of another person.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A person who compiles dictionaries"
questions.explanation: The word is "lexicographer": one who compiles dictionaries. The other options mean: cartographer: one who draws or makes maps; biographer: one who writes the life story of another person; calligrapher: an expert in beautiful handwriting.

questions.questionText: Which one word stands for "A person who is an expert in beautiful handwriting"?
questions.explanation: The word is "calligrapher": an expert in beautiful handwriting. The other options mean: stenographer: one who writes in shorthand; graphologist: an expert who studies handwriting to judge a person's character; cryptographer: one who writes or designs secret codes.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A person who designs or solves secret codes"
questions.explanation: The word is "cryptographer": one who writes or designs secret codes. The other options mean: stenographer: one who writes in shorthand; lexicographer: one who compiles dictionaries; calligrapher: an expert in beautiful handwriting.

questions.questionText: What is the one-word substitute for: "A doctor who specialises in diseases of the kidneys"?
questions.explanation: The word is "nephrologist": a doctor who specialises in diseases of the kidneys. The other options mean: hepatologist: a doctor who specialises in diseases of the liver; gastroenterologist: a doctor who specialises in diseases of the stomach and intestines; cardiologist: a doctor who specialises in diseases of the heart.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A dentist who corrects teeth that are irregularly placed"
questions.explanation: The word is "orthodontist": a dentist who corrects irregularly placed teeth. The other options mean: chiropodist: one who treats minor ailments of the feet; orthopaedist: a doctor who treats disorders of the bones and joints; paediatrician: a doctor who treats children's diseases.

questions.questionText: Which one word stands for "A doctor who specialises in the care of elderly people"?
questions.explanation: The word is "geriatrician": a doctor who treats the diseases of old people. The other options mean: paediatrician: a doctor who treats children's diseases; psychiatrist: a doctor who treats mental illness; radiologist: a doctor who diagnoses illness using X-rays and scans.

questions.questionText: What is the one-word substitute for: "A scientist who studies the origin and development of mankind and its customs"?
questions.explanation: The word is "anthropologist": a scientist who studies the origin, development and customs of mankind. The other options mean: archaeologist: one who studies ancient civilisations through excavated remains; ornithologist: a scientist who studies birds; entomologist: a scientist who studies insects.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A person who studies ancient civilisations by digging up and examining their remains"
questions.explanation: The word is "archaeologist": one who studies ancient civilisations through excavated remains. The other options mean: ornithologist: a scientist who studies birds; geologist: a scientist who studies the earth's rocks and structure; linguist: one who studies language scientifically.

questions.questionText: Which one word stands for "A scientist who studies insects"?
questions.explanation: The word is "entomologist": a scientist who studies insects. The other options mean: ornithologist: a scientist who studies birds; etymologist: one who studies the origin and historical development of words; herpetologist: a scientist who studies reptiles and amphibians.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A person who knows or speaks many languages"
questions.explanation: The word is "polyglot": a person who knows or speaks many languages. The other options mean: orator: a skilled public speaker; pedant: a person who makes a show of learning or is overly concerned with minor rules; elocutionist: an expert in the art of clear and effective speaking.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A teacher or schoolmaster"
questions.explanation: The word is "pedagogue": a teacher or schoolmaster. The other options mean: pedant: a person who makes a show of learning or is overly concerned with minor rules; demagogue: a political leader who wins support by appealing to popular passions and prejudices; pedlar: a person who sells small goods by going from door to door.
questions.shortcut: Paid- (child) + agogos (leader): leads children, a teacher.

questions.questionText: What is the one-word substitute for: "A ruler who holds absolute power"?
questions.explanation: The word is "autocrat": a ruler with absolute power. The other options mean: democrat: a believer in rule by the people; bureaucrat: an official in a government department; aristocrat: a member of the hereditary noble class.

questions.questionText: Which one word stands for "A person who practises severe self-discipline and avoids worldly pleasures"?
questions.explanation: The word is "ascetic": a person who lives a life of severe self-discipline and avoids worldly pleasures. The other options mean: epicure: a person who takes refined pleasure in good food and drink; hedonist: a person who believes that pleasure is the chief aim of life; sceptic: a person who doubts accepted opinions.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A person who does an activity for love of it and not for money"
questions.explanation: The word is "amateur": a person who takes part in an activity for love of it, not for money. The other options mean: professional: a person who earns a living from an activity; veteran: a person with long experience, especially an ex-soldier; pedant: a person who makes a show of learning or is overly concerned with minor rules.

questions.questionText: What is the one-word substitute for: "An expert who studies a person's handwriting to judge his character"?
questions.explanation: The word is "graphologist": an expert who studies handwriting to judge a person's character. The other options mean: calligrapher: an expert in beautiful handwriting; palmist: one who tells fortunes by reading the lines of the palm; phrenologist: one who studies the shape of the skull to judge character.

questions.questionText: What is the one-word substitute for: "A person who studies the origin and historical development of words"?
questions.explanation: The word is "etymologist": one who studies the origin and historical development of words. The other options mean: entomologist: a scientist who studies insects; ornithologist: a scientist who studies birds; ethnologist: one who studies the different races of people and their cultures.

questions.questionText: Which one word stands for "A political leader who wins power by appealing to the emotions and prejudices of the common people"?
questions.explanation: The word is "demagogue": a political leader who wins support by appealing to popular passions and prejudices. The other options mean: pedagogue: a teacher or schoolmaster; democrat: a believer in rule by the people; bureaucrat: an official in a government department.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A person whose power or influence comes from his great wealth"
questions.explanation: The word is "plutocrat": a person whose power comes from his wealth. The other options mean: aristocrat: a member of the hereditary noble class; democrat: a believer in rule by the people; bureaucrat: an official in a government department.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A person who takes refined pleasure in good food and drink"
questions.explanation: The word is "epicure": a person who takes refined pleasure in good food and drink. The other options mean: glutton: a person who eats greedily and too much; ascetic: a person who lives a life of severe self-discipline and avoids worldly pleasures; cynic: a person who distrusts the motives of others.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "An abnormal fear of confined or closed spaces"
questions.explanation: The word is "claustrophobia": abnormal fear of confined or closed spaces. The other options mean: agoraphobia: abnormal fear of open or crowded public places; acrophobia: abnormal fear of heights; hydrophobia: abnormal fear of water.

questions.questionText: Which one word stands for "An abnormal fear of heights"?
questions.explanation: The word is "acrophobia": abnormal fear of heights. The other options mean: hydrophobia: abnormal fear of water; claustrophobia: abnormal fear of confined or closed spaces; photophobia: abnormal dread of, or sensitivity to, light.

questions.questionText: What is the one-word substitute for: "An abnormal fear of water"?
questions.explanation: The word is "hydrophobia": abnormal fear of water. The other options mean: acrophobia: abnormal fear of heights; pyrophobia: abnormal fear of fire; xenophobia: fear or hatred of strangers and foreigners.

questions.questionText: Which one word stands for "The scientific study of fish"?
questions.explanation: The word is "ichthyology": the scientific study of fish. The other options mean: ornithology: the scientific study of birds; herpetology: the scientific study of reptiles and amphibians; mycology: the scientific study of fungi.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "The scientific study of earthquakes"
questions.explanation: The word is "seismology": the scientific study of earthquakes. The other options mean: meteorology: the scientific study of weather and the atmosphere; geology: the scientific study of the earth's rocks and structure; oceanography: the study of the oceans.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "The scientific study of weather and the atmosphere"
questions.explanation: The word is "meteorology": the scientific study of weather and the atmosphere. The other options mean: seismology: the scientific study of earthquakes; hydrology: the scientific study of water and its movement over and under the earth; astronomy: the scientific study of celestial bodies.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "The study of God and religious belief"
questions.explanation: The word is "theology": the study of God and religious belief. The other options mean: mythology: a body of myths, or the study of myths; philosophy: the study of the fundamental nature of knowledge, reality and existence; ideology: a system of ideas and ideals.

questions.questionText: Which one word stands for "The scientific study of the earth's rocks and structure"?
questions.explanation: The word is "geology": the scientific study of the earth's rocks and structure. The other options mean: genealogy: the study of family descent and lineage; ecology: the study of how living things relate to one another and to their environment; geometry: the branch of mathematics dealing with shapes and sizes.

questions.questionText: What is the one-word substitute for: "The scientific study of animals"?
questions.explanation: The word is "zoology": the scientific study of animals. The other options mean: botany: the scientific study of plants; geology: the scientific study of the earth's rocks and structure; mycology: the scientific study of fungi.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "The scientific study of plants"
questions.explanation: The word is "botany": the scientific study of plants. The other options mean: zoology: the scientific study of animals; geology: the scientific study of the earth's rocks and structure; genealogy: the study of family descent and lineage.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "An abnormal fear of open or crowded public places"
questions.explanation: The word is "agoraphobia": abnormal fear of open or crowded public places. The other options mean: claustrophobia: abnormal fear of confined or closed spaces; xenophobia: fear or hatred of strangers and foreigners; acrophobia: abnormal fear of heights.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A fear or hatred of strangers and foreigners"
questions.explanation: The word is "xenophobia": fear or hatred of strangers and foreigners. The other options mean: technophobia: fear or dislike of advanced technology; agoraphobia: abnormal fear of open or crowded public places; hydrophobia: abnormal fear of water.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "An abnormal dread of, or sensitivity to, light"
questions.explanation: The word is "photophobia": abnormal dread of, or sensitivity to, light. The other options mean: nyctophobia: abnormal fear of darkness or night; claustrophobia: abnormal fear of confined or closed spaces; acrophobia: abnormal fear of heights.

questions.questionText: Which one word stands for "An abnormal fear of fire"?
questions.explanation: The word is "pyrophobia": abnormal fear of fire. The other options mean: hydrophobia: abnormal fear of water; haemophobia: abnormal fear of blood; acrophobia: abnormal fear of heights.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "An abnormal fear of blood"
questions.explanation: The word is "haemophobia": abnormal fear of blood. The other options mean: hydrophobia: abnormal fear of water; pyrophobia: abnormal fear of fire; technophobia: fear or dislike of advanced technology.

questions.questionText: Which one word stands for "A fear or dislike of advanced technology and machines"?
questions.explanation: The word is "technophobia": fear or dislike of advanced technology. The other options mean: xenophobia: fear or hatred of strangers and foreigners; haemophobia: abnormal fear of blood; claustrophobia: abnormal fear of confined or closed spaces.

questions.questionText: What is the one-word substitute for: "The scientific study of reptiles and amphibians"?
questions.explanation: The word is "herpetology": the scientific study of reptiles and amphibians. The other options mean: ichthyology: the scientific study of fish; ornithology: the scientific study of birds; mycology: the scientific study of fungi.

questions.questionText: Which one word stands for "The scientific study of fungi"?
questions.explanation: The word is "mycology": the scientific study of fungi. The other options mean: botany: the scientific study of plants; zoology: the scientific study of animals; ichthyology: the scientific study of fish.

questions.questionText: What is the one-word substitute for: "The study of family descent and lineage"?
questions.explanation: The word is "genealogy": the study of family descent and lineage. The other options mean: geology: the scientific study of the earth's rocks and structure; genetics: the study of heredity and genes; geography: the study of the earth's surface, climate and people.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "The branch of medicine that deals with the study and treatment of cancer"
questions.explanation: The word is "oncology": the study and treatment of cancer. The other options mean: cardiology: the study and treatment of heart diseases; pathology: the study of the causes and nature of diseases; neurology: the study of the nervous system.

questions.questionText: What is the one-word substitute for: "The study of how living things are related to one another and to their surroundings"?
questions.explanation: The word is "ecology": the study of how living things relate to one another and to their environment. The other options mean: zoology: the scientific study of animals; ethology: the study of animal behaviour; geology: the scientific study of the earth's rocks and structure.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "The scientific study of water and its movement over and under the earth"
questions.explanation: The word is "hydrology": the scientific study of water and its movement over and under the earth. The other options mean: geology: the scientific study of the earth's rocks and structure; seismology: the scientific study of earthquakes; cartography: the science of drawing maps.

questions.questionText: What is the one-word substitute for: "An abnormal fear of spiders"?
questions.explanation: The word is "arachnophobia": abnormal fear of spiders. The other options mean: ophidiophobia: abnormal fear of snakes; cynophobia: abnormal fear of dogs; ailurophobia: abnormal fear of cats.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "An abnormal fear of dogs"
questions.explanation: The word is "cynophobia": abnormal fear of dogs. The other options mean: ailurophobia: abnormal fear of cats; arachnophobia: abnormal fear of spiders; ophidiophobia: abnormal fear of snakes.

questions.questionText: What is the one-word substitute for: "An abnormal fear of darkness or night"?
questions.explanation: The word is "nyctophobia": abnormal fear of darkness or night. The other options mean: photophobia: abnormal dread of, or sensitivity to, light; claustrophobia: abnormal fear of confined or closed spaces; acrophobia: abnormal fear of heights.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "An abnormal fear of the number thirteen"
questions.explanation: The word is "triskaidekaphobia": abnormal fear of the number thirteen. The other options mean: xenophobia: fear or hatred of strangers and foreigners; arachnophobia: abnormal fear of spiders; acrophobia: abnormal fear of heights.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "An abnormal fear of snakes"
questions.explanation: The word is "ophidiophobia": abnormal fear of snakes. The other options mean: arachnophobia: abnormal fear of spiders; cynophobia: abnormal fear of dogs; pyrophobia: abnormal fear of fire.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "The study of the causes and nature of diseases"
questions.explanation: The word is "pathology": the study of the causes and nature of diseases. The other options mean: oncology: the study and treatment of cancer; physiology: the study of the normal functioning of living organisms; pharmacology: the study of drugs and their effects.

questions.questionText: Which one word stands for "The study of fossils and the life of ancient geological periods"?
questions.explanation: The word is "palaeontology": the study of fossils and the life of ancient geological periods. The other options mean: archaeology: the study of human history through excavated remains; geology: the scientific study of the earth's rocks and structure; anthropology: the study of human origins, societies and cultures.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "The study of poisons and their effects"
questions.explanation: The word is "toxicology": the study of poisons and their effects. The other options mean: pharmacology: the study of drugs and their effects; pathology: the study of the causes and nature of diseases; physiology: the study of the normal functioning of living organisms.

questions.questionText: Which one word stands for "The science of measuring time and the art of making clocks and watches"?
questions.explanation: The word is "horology": the science of measuring time and the art of making clocks and watches. The other options mean: horticulture: the art of growing gardens, flowers and vegetables; numismatics: the study or collection of coins; cryptography: the art of writing or solving secret codes.

questions.questionText: What is the one-word substitute for: "The study of people's efficiency and comfort in their working environment"?
questions.explanation: The word is "ergonomics": the study of people's efficiency and comfort in their working environment. The other options mean: economics: the study of production, trade and wealth; ecology: the study of how living things relate to one another and to their environment; ethology: the study of animal behaviour.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A group of lions"
questions.explanation: The word is "pride": the collective noun for lions. Do not confuse it with "herd": a group of cattle, elephants or deer.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A group of wolves or hunting dogs"
questions.explanation: The word is "pack": the collective noun for wolves or hounds. Do not confuse it with "pride": a group of lions.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "A group of sheep"
questions.explanation: The word is "flock": the collective noun for sheep, and also for birds. Do not confuse it with "pride": a group of lions.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "A group of cattle or elephants"
questions.explanation: The word is "herd": the collective noun for cattle and elephants. Do not confuse it with "flock": a group of sheep or birds.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A group of fish swimming together"
questions.explanation: The word is "shoal": the collective noun for fish. Do not confuse it with "swarm": a large group of flying insects such as bees.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A group of bees flying together"
questions.explanation: The word is "swarm": the collective noun for bees and other flying insects. Do not confuse it with "shoal": a group of fish.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "A group of singers performing together"
questions.explanation: The word is "choir": an organised group of singers. Do not confuse it with "orchestra": a group of instrumentalists.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A group of musicians playing different instruments together"
questions.explanation: The word is "orchestra": a large group of instrumentalists. Do not confuse it with "choir": a group of singers.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "A number of grapes growing together"
questions.explanation: The word is "bunch": a cluster of fruit such as grapes or bananas on one stem. Do not confuse it with "flock": a group of animals, especially sheep.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A group of cards used in a game"
questions.explanation: The word is "pack": a complete set of playing cards. Do not confuse it with "bunch": things growing together on a stem.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A group of players forming one side in a game"
questions.explanation: The word is "team": a group of players forming one side in a sport. Do not confuse it with "gang": a group of criminals acting together.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "A group of ships sailing together under one command"
questions.explanation: The word is "fleet": a number of ships under one command. Do not confuse it with "squad": a small group of soldiers or workers.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A group of newborn puppies or kittens born at one time"
questions.explanation: The word is "litter": the young born to an animal at one birth. Do not confuse it with "brood": the young birds hatched together.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "A group of eggs laid or hatched at one time"
questions.explanation: The word is "clutch": a set of eggs laid by a bird in one nest. Do not confuse it with "litter": the young born to a mammal at one birth.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "A group of young birds hatched together and cared for by the mother"
questions.explanation: The word is "brood": the young birds hatched at one time. Do not confuse it with "litter": the young of mammals born at one birth.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A group of stars forming a recognised pattern in the sky"
questions.explanation: The word is "constellation": a named pattern of stars. Do not confuse it with "galaxy": a vast system of millions of stars.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A group of steps between two floors"
questions.explanation: The word is "flight": a series of stairs between landings. Do not confuse it with "fleet": a group of ships.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "The people who work together on a ship or aircraft"
questions.explanation: The word is "crew": the people operating a ship, aircraft or train. Do not confuse it with "staff": the permanent employees of an organisation.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "A group of people gathered to hear a speaker or performance"
questions.explanation: The word is "audience": the people attending a performance or speech to listen. Do not confuse it with "mob": a large disorderly crowd.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "A group of worshippers gathered in a place of worship"
questions.explanation: The word is "congregation": a group assembled for religious worship. Do not confuse it with "audience": people gathered to listen to or watch a performance.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A group of officers chosen to conduct some business on behalf of a larger body"
questions.explanation: The word is "committee": a group appointed to carry out a specific task. Do not confuse it with "audience": people gathered to listen or watch.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "A group of mountains forming a connected chain"
questions.explanation: The word is "range": a line of connected mountains. Do not confuse it with "cluster": a number of similar things close together.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "A group of islands"
questions.explanation: The word is "archipelago": a chain or cluster of islands. Do not confuse it with "peninsula": a piece of land almost surrounded by water.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A group of travellers or merchants journeying together across a desert"
questions.explanation: The word is "caravan": a company travelling together through desert or hazardous country. Do not confuse it with "fleet": a number of ships under one command.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A large number of people gathered together in a disorderly manner"
questions.explanation: The word is "mob": a large disorderly crowd. Do not confuse it with "audience": people gathered to hear a performance.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "A group of criminals or hooligans acting together"
questions.explanation: The word is "gang": a group of people, often criminals, acting together. Do not confuse it with "pack": a group of wolves or hunting dogs.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "The employees who work in an office, school or hospital"
questions.explanation: The word is "staff": the people employed by an organisation. Do not confuse it with "crew": the people operating a ship or aircraft.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "A group of actors performing together on stage"
questions.explanation: The word is "troupe": a company of actors or performers. Do not confuse it with "troop": a group of soldiers or scouts.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A group of soldiers, especially on the march"
questions.explanation: The word is "troop": a body of soldiers or scouts. Do not confuse it with "troupe": a company of actors or acrobats.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A group of geese flying in a V-formation"
questions.explanation: The word is "skein": a flight of geese or wild fowl in the air. Do not confuse it with "gaggle": geese on the ground, a noisy group.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "A group of geese on the ground"
questions.explanation: The word is "gaggle": a collective noun for geese when they are not flying. Do not confuse it with "skein": geese flying in formation.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "A group of owls"
questions.explanation: The word is "parliament": the traditional collective noun for owls. Do not confuse it with "senate": a ruling body, not a group of birds.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A group of crows"
questions.explanation: The word is "murder": the traditional collective noun for crows. Do not confuse it with "flock": the collective noun for lions.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A number of cattle or sheep driven together"
questions.explanation: The word is "drove": a number of cattle or sheep driven in a body. Do not confuse it with "troupe": a company of actors.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "The quality of being brave"
questions.explanation: The word is "bravery": the quality of courage in the face of danger. Do not confuse it with "bravado": a show of boldness meant to impress.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "The state of being a child"
questions.explanation: The word is "childhood": the period or state of being a child. Do not confuse it with "boyhood": the period of being a boy only.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "The quality of being honest"
questions.explanation: The word is "honesty": truthfulness and freedom from deceit. Do not confuse it with "honour": high respect or good name.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "The quality of being generous"
questions.explanation: The word is "generosity": willingness to give freely. Do not confuse it with "geniality": friendly cheerfulness.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "Strong dislike or ill will towards another"
questions.explanation: The word is "hatred": intense dislike or ill will. Do not confuse it with "anger": a feeling of strong annoyance.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "The quality of being wise"
questions.explanation: The word is "wisdom": good judgement based on knowledge and experience. Do not confuse it with "wit": quick and inventive humour.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "The state of being friends with someone"
questions.explanation: The word is "friendship": the bond or state of being friends. Do not confuse it with "friction": conflict or rubbing between persons or surfaces.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "The quality of being able to do something well"
questions.explanation: The word is "ability": the power or skill to do something. Do not confuse it with "agility": quickness and ease of movement.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "The condition of being healthy"
questions.explanation: The word is "health": the state of being free from illness. Do not confuse it with "wealth": abundance of money or possessions.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "The feeling of discontent at another's good fortune"
questions.explanation: The word is "envy": resentful longing for what another has. Do not confuse it with "pride": sorrow felt for the suffering of others.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "The quality of being loyal to a person or cause"
questions.explanation: The word is "loyalty": firm and constant support or allegiance. Do not confuse it with "royalty": the status of a king or queen.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "The quality of being modest and not proud"
questions.explanation: The word is "humility": a modest view of one's own importance. Do not confuse it with "humour": the quality of being amusing.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "The state of being able to bear pain or delay calmly"
questions.explanation: The word is "patience": the capacity to endure delay or hardship calmly. Do not confuse it with "patronage": support given by a patron.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "The strong desire to possess more than one needs"
questions.explanation: The word is "greed": intense selfish desire for wealth or possessions. Do not confuse it with "grief": deep sorrow, especially at a loss.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "The state of being exact and free from error"
questions.explanation: The word is "accuracy": exactness and freedom from error. Do not confuse it with "agility": quickness and ease of movement.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "The state of perfect happiness"
questions.explanation: The word is "bliss": perfect happiness; great joy. Do not confuse it with "bias": an unfair leaning towards one side.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "The state of being a slave"
questions.explanation: The word is "slavery": the state of being owned by another and forced to labour. Do not confuse it with "slavishness": excessive servility in character.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "The state of being a widow"
questions.explanation: The word is "widowhood": the condition of a woman whose husband has died. Do not confuse it with "spinsterhood": the state of being an unmarried woman.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "The state of being free from all trouble and anxiety"
questions.explanation: The word is "serenity": a state of calm and peace. Do not confuse it with "solitude": the state of being alone.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "The state of being poor"
questions.explanation: The word is "poverty": the state of lacking money and basic necessities. Do not confuse it with "prosperity": a state of wealth and success.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "The quality of being proud of oneself in an excessive manner"
questions.explanation: The word is "arrogance": an offensive display of superiority. Do not confuse it with "ambition": a strong desire to achieve something.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "The quality of being thankful"
questions.explanation: The word is "gratitude": the quality of being thankful. Do not confuse it with "gratuity": a sum of money paid on retirement or a tip.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "The state of being an adult male"
questions.explanation: The word is "manhood": the state of being an adult male. Do not confuse it with "mankind": the human race as a whole.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "The quality of being kind and gentle to those in distress"
questions.explanation: The word is "compassion": sympathy and concern for the sufferings of others. Do not confuse it with "compulsion": a force that compels one to act.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "The habit of avoiding spending or giving too much money"
questions.explanation: The word is "thrift": careful and economical use of money. Do not confuse it with "theft": the act of stealing.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "The state of being a member of a club or society"
questions.explanation: The word is "membership": the state of belonging to a group or society. Do not confuse it with "friendship": the bond between friends.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "The state of having no money to pay one's debts"
questions.explanation: The word is "bankruptcy": the legal state of being unable to pay one's debts. Do not confuse it with "poverty": the state of having very little money, not necessarily owing debts.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "The quality of being very careful to avoid risk or error"
questions.explanation: The word is "caution": care taken to avoid danger or mistakes. Do not confuse it with "cowardice": lack of courage in the face of danger.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "The quality of being punctual"
questions.explanation: The word is "punctuality": the habit of being on time. Do not confuse it with "perseverance": steady effort despite difficulties.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "The state of being dependent on a drug or habit"
questions.explanation: The word is "addiction": compulsive dependence on a substance or activity. Do not confuse it with "affliction": a condition of suffering or distress.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "The legal status of being a citizen of a country"
questions.explanation: The word is "citizenship": the legal status of being a citizen. Do not confuse it with "citation": an official quotation or a mention for bravery.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "The act of telling a lie under oath in a court of law"
questions.explanation: The word is "perjury": deliberately telling an untruth after taking an oath. Do not confuse it with "forgery": the act of making a false document.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "That which cannot be read because it is badly written"
questions.explanation: The word is "illegible": not clear enough to be read. Do not confuse it with "inaudible": not loud enough to be heard.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "That which cannot be avoided"
questions.explanation: The word is "inevitable": certain to happen; unavoidable. Do not confuse it with "incredible": too extraordinary to be believed.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "The life story of a person written by that person"
questions.explanation: The word is "autobiography": a person's life story written by himself or herself. Do not confuse it with "biography": a life story written by someone else.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "Fit to be eaten"
questions.explanation: The word is "edible": safe and fit to be eaten. Do not confuse it with "eligible": qualified to be chosen.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A fixed sum of money paid regularly to a person after retirement"
questions.explanation: The word is "pension": a regular payment made to a retired person. Do not confuse it with "pittance": a very small amount of money.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "A building where grain is stored"
questions.explanation: The word is "granary": a storehouse for grain. Do not confuse it with "armoury": a place where weapons are stored.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "Done of one's own free will"
questions.explanation: The word is "voluntary": done by choice, not by compulsion. Do not confuse it with "compulsory": required by rule.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "That which cannot be seen"
questions.explanation: The word is "invisible": unable to be seen. Do not confuse it with "inaudible": unable to be heard.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "That which cannot be heard"
questions.explanation: The word is "inaudible": unable to be heard. Do not confuse it with "invisible": unable to be seen.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A school or institution where children without parents are looked after"
questions.explanation: The word is "orphanage": an institution caring for children without parents. Do not confuse it with "hospice": a home caring for the terminally ill.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A speech delivered without any preparation"
questions.explanation: The word is "extempore": spoken or done without preparation. Do not confuse it with "monologue": a long speech by one person in a conversation or play.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "A person or habit that cannot be corrected"
questions.explanation: The word is "incorrigible": not able to be corrected or reformed. Do not confuse it with "incurable": not able to be healed of a disease.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "Government by a small group of people"
questions.explanation: The word is "oligarchy": rule by a few. Do not confuse it with "democracy": rule by the people through elected representatives.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "Present everywhere at the same time"
questions.explanation: The word is "omnipresent": present in all places at once. Do not confuse it with "omniscient": knowing everything.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "The killing of a king"
questions.explanation: The word is "regicide": the act of killing a king. Do not confuse it with "fratricide": the killing of one's brother.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "A large cage or house in which birds are kept"
questions.explanation: The word is "aviary": a place where birds are kept. Do not confuse it with "apiary": a place where bees are kept.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "Something that can never be satisfied"
questions.explanation: The word is "insatiable": impossible to satisfy. Do not confuse it with "insolvent": unable to pay one's debts.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "A home or centre that cares for the terminally ill"
questions.explanation: The word is "hospice": a place caring for the dying. Do not confuse it with "hospital": an institution for treating the sick and injured generally.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "A person who is unable to pay his debts"
questions.explanation: The word is "insolvent": unable to pay one's debts. Do not confuse it with "insomniac": a person who cannot sleep.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "A remedy for all diseases"
questions.explanation: The word is "panacea": a cure for all ills. Do not confuse it with "antidote": a medicine that counteracts a poison.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A substance that counteracts the effect of a poison"
questions.explanation: The word is "antidote": a remedy that works against a poison. Do not confuse it with "panacea": a supposed cure for all diseases.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "One who knows everything"
questions.explanation: The word is "omniscient": all-knowing. Do not confuse it with "omnipresent": present everywhere.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "The killing of one's own father"
questions.explanation: The word is "patricide": the act of killing one's father. Do not confuse it with "matricide": the killing of one's mother.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "The killing of one's own brother or sister"
questions.explanation: The word is "fratricide": the act of killing a brother or sister. Do not confuse it with "patricide": the killing of one's father.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "Lasting for a very short time"
questions.explanation: The word is "ephemeral": short-lived. Do not confuse it with "eternal": lasting forever.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A person who leaves his country to live permanently in another"
questions.explanation: The word is "emigrant": a person who leaves his own country to settle elsewhere. Do not confuse it with "immigrant": a person who comes into a country to settle there.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "A person who comes to settle permanently in a foreign country"
questions.explanation: The word is "immigrant": a person who comes to live permanently in another country. Do not confuse it with "emigrant": a person who leaves his own country to settle elsewhere.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "A place where dead bodies are kept before burial or cremation"
questions.explanation: The word is "mortuary": a place where dead bodies are kept temporarily. Do not confuse it with "cemetery": a place where bodies are buried.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A system of government carried out by officials who are not elected"
questions.explanation: The word is "bureaucracy": administration by appointed officials. Do not confuse it with "autocracy": rule by one person with absolute power.

questions.questionText: Choose the one word that can replace the phrase: "A speech by one character alone on the stage speaking his thoughts aloud"
questions.explanation: The word is "soliloquy": speaking one's thoughts aloud when alone, especially in a play. Do not confuse it with "monologue": a long speech by one person addressed to others.

questions.questionText: Pick the one word that stands for: "A person who has personally seen a crime or accident and can testify about it"
questions.explanation: The word is "eyewitness": a person who has personally seen an event, especially a crime or accident. Do not confuse it with "accomplice": a person who helps another commit a crime.

questions.questionText: Which one word can be used in place of the phrase: "A handwriting that is difficult to read or a document that cannot be understood"
questions.explanation: The word is "indecipherable": impossible to read or understand. Do not confuse it with "illiterate": unable to read or write.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A medicine or treatment that prevents the occurrence of a disease"
questions.explanation: The word is "preventive": intended to stop something from happening. Do not confuse it with "curative": intended to heal an existing illness.

questions.questionText: Select the single word that best substitutes for: "A medicine that relieves pain without curing the disease"
questions.explanation: The word is "palliative": easing pain or a problem without removing its cause. Do not confuse it with "preventive": stopping something from happening.
